hints: Start by thinking in moles, not grams, since the balanced equation tells us about mole ratios.
Work out moles of each known substance: 2.0 g of $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ ($M_r = 80$) and 0.90 g of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($M_r = 18$).
Use your 1 to 2 ratio to balance N, H and O atoms and see which nitrogen-containing gas fits perfectly.
walkthrough:
**Convert masses to moles**

Lovely, let's turn what we can weigh into what we can count. Moles link mass to the equation.

$$\text{moles} = \frac{\text{mass}}{M_r}$$

$$\text{moles of NH}_4\text{NO}_3 = \frac{2.0}{80} = 0.025 \text{ mol}$$

$$\text{moles of H}_2\text{O} = \frac{0.90}{18} = 0.050 \text{ mol}$$

**Find the mole ratio**

Now compare them side by side to see the pattern.

$$\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 : \text{H}_2\text{O} = 0.025 : 0.050 = 1 : 2$$

So 1 mole of ammonium nitrate produces 2 moles of water.

**Use atom balance to identify the gas**

Think of atoms as building blocks that must be conserved. We start with $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ which contains $\text{N}_2$, $\text{H}_4$ and $\text{O}_3$.

If we make $2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, that already uses up all $\text{H}_4$ and $\text{O}_2$. We are left with $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{O}_1$ to make the gas.

$$\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

That balances perfectly, so the single gas must be dinitrogen oxide, $\text{N}_2\text{O}$.

options.A: NO would give $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NO} + ...$ which cannot balance H and O to give a 1 to 2 ratio with water. It leaves N and O atoms unbalanced.
options.B: NO2 contains only one N atom, so forming it plus 2 waters would leave N and O unbalanced. It is also a common trap because nitrogen dioxide is a well known gas from nitrate decomposition, but not from this reaction.
options.C: N2O is correct because $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ balances for all atoms and matches the observed 1:2 mole ratio (0.025 mol to 0.050 mol).
options.D: N2 contains no oxygen, so all 3 O atoms would have to be in water. That would need 3 waters, not 2, which contradicts the 0.90 g (0.05 mol) of water found.
